themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score 6.35), suggesting either a sudden enforcement crack or unauthorized vendor proliferation in Sunset Park that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically anomalous event
Spike appeared in most recent reporting period, not lagged data
reporting_angles: Are vendors unlicensed or operating in restricted areas? Contact NYC Health for enforcement activity.
Interview residents near hotspots—are there quality/sanitation concerns driving complaints?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 49 LAST WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly average (263% increase, z-score 6.56), indicating a potential new source of disruption—construction, nightlife, or commercial operation—that requires street-level verification.
evidence: 49 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly average (263% spike)
No corresponding spike in residential noise, suggesting concentrated commercial source
reporting_angles: Map the 49 complaints geographically—is the noise clustered near a bar, construction site, or new venue?
Interview affected residents and business owners; cross-reference with DOB permits for recent commercial approvals or construction.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Vandalism Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints reached 31 LAST WEEK vs. 9.1 weekly average (240% increase, z-score 5.29), marking the second-highest spike this period and potentially indicating organized vandalism activity or breakdown in sanitation enforcement.
evidence: 31 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 9.1 weekly baseline (240% increase)
Sustained spike in last week suggests active pattern, not isolated incident
reporting_angles: Request NYPD gang intelligence and Parks Dept. response logs to determine if this is gang-related or copycat vandalism.
Photograph affected areas and interview residents—has there been visible increase in tags in specific neighborhoods?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Alert
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints peaked at 6 THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 11.0, highest z-score in dataset), though data is now 3 weeks old; urgent follow-up needed to confirm if spike has persisted or resolved.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (1100% spike)
Highest z-score in entire dataset (11.0), indicating most anomalous signal
Data lag means current status unknown—urgent need to verify if spike continues
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD 72nd Precinct for arrest/activity logs from 3 weeks ago and current status. Has the spike resolved or is it ongoing?
Interview residents and local business owners in affected areas about visibility of drug use/dealing. Cross-check with community board if this was flagged.

themes_detail.label: Building-Related Complaints Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Three separate building-related spikes converged LAST WEEK: Boilers (3 complaints vs. 0.2 avg), Outside Building (3 complaints vs. 0.2 avg), and General conditions (22 complaints vs. 5.2 avg), totaling 28 complaints across housing/maintenance issues—suggesting either seasonal heating failure or systematic building code violations.
evidence: Boiler complaints: 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 baseline (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Outside Building complaints: 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 baseline (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
General complaints: 22 LAST WEEK vs. 5.2 baseline (319% increase, z-score 7.18)
Combined 28 building-related complaints suggest systemic rather than isolated issue
reporting_angles: Contact HPD and NYCHA: Are there known heating outages or boiler failures in Sunset Park buildings? Request inspection data.
Interview tenants in affected buildings about heat/hot water access (note: 637 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days already, now accelerating). Identify landlords with multiple complaints.
